items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

ctx.x: Correct. But not mockery or whatever the word is.

That’s macabre. Don’t laugh. It’s just as macabre in jazz life too, to see all these Charlie Parker clones come out. Did you ever hear of the guys who try to emulate Louis where they, Armstrong, where they really fail is when they try to do the vocalizations. Then it becomes a travesty, like the Elvis. Because that’s where they fail. Unless they just use their own natural voice. items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But when he first came out I didn’t think very much of his music at all, in fact we hated it.

ctx.x: Well I mean I look back, I look at him now and I almost shed a tear. When he first came out I remember I was working with Tony Spargo who was the original drummer with the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, right? And he says, “Oh y’all are just jeal—” he had a southern, New Orleans accent, he said, “y’all are just jealous of him because he’s got such a pretty face.” But when he first came out I didn’t think very much of his music at all, in fact we hated it. It was gyrations and obscene, and there we are, very staid…
